test_policy.notes: International FAQ: SAT/ACT are not required for admission; admissibility rests on the transcript-based U.S.-equivalent GPA (generally 3.0+ on a U.S.-weighted 4.0 scale). SAT/ACT may satisfy English proficiency (SAT EBRW 500+, ACT English 21+) and placement.

requirements.notes: Apply with the Millersville application or the Common App. The FAQ says international applicants pay no application fee. Unofficial transcripts are uploaded with the application; International Admissions evaluates them to a U.S. GPA. First-year students must live on campus unless they qualify for a waiver.

deadlines.label: Advisory international deadline, fall 2027
deadlines.notes: Rolling admission with no strict deadline; the page advises applying at least two months before term start for visa processing and gives the advisory date as Fall - June 1 (no year printed, treated as 2027). Spring: November 1.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Waived with a U.S. associate degree, full IB Diploma in English, a high school diploma and/or citizenship from a listed English-speaking country, one full U.S. high school year with C or better in standard English, GCSE/GCE English C or better, IB English score 4+, or WAEC C6+. Test scores must be under 2 years old (SAT/ACT within 5 years). Applicants without an admissible score may apply for Conditional Admission and start at the English Language Institute.

english.notes: The page lists no new-scale (1-6) TOEFL score.
IELTS Academic overall band 6.0 with no subscore lower than 5.

aid.notes: Millersville's admissions-scholarships page lists an 'International Scholarships' contact (717-871-7506, international@millersville.edu). Award names and amounts could not be confirmed: the international financial-assistance page was unreachable (404) when checked, so scholarship amounts are left null. Confirm with International Admissions.

cost.notes: International estimated annual proof-of-funding for 2026-2027: tuition and fees $17,620 (includes some mandatory fees; 12-18 credits per semester), living expenses $13,890, health insurance $750, books and miscellaneous $1,400, total $33,660. A separate $150 per semester international student fee ($300 per year) is charged in addition and is not in that total.
